searchText: This is reasonable question. Suppose, EL moves to a separate shard, an execution payload will contain the root of a beacon block it's built upon. Which already implies some dependency, even minimal, but it seems unavoidable. And verifying this root implies running a beacon chain node, potentially a light client node. And we might want to avoid dependencies going beyond the light client -- this sounds like a reasonable boundary for how far we want to go with tying two layers. Could you please point me to the forum where this kind of recovery mechanism has been proposed? August: https://ethresear.ch/t/preparing-withdrawals-for-compromised-validator-or-withdrawal-keys-fao-zilm/10453 Mostly just discussions/questions around "is it possible (to save my funds)?!": A somewhat long discussion on this server on the 24th/25th of September https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/748530848470663208/890887578335707146 https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/748530848470663208/891170083819372604 In April over in the Ethstaker discord: https://discord.com/channels/694822223575384095/749027200837353512/795692435492831252 and yesterday: https://discord.com/channels/694822223575384095/694822223575384099/918681969280290827 (There's probably more instances of people asking/worrying about this, but those are the ones I could find in a few minutes) Thank you so much for this thorough answer I like this. The work for people who are worried would be to propose a mechanism that allows them to verify they are legit, maybe by showing control of the deposit wallet. And then the dot txt could be restricting the 00->01 change to just the eoa of the deposit wallet. Someone who lost control of both deposit wallet and validator mnemonic, I don’t know a reasonable way to prove ownership. <@!397389662085185547> Are you in contact with people who are impacted? I am thinking they need to form a group; propose a solid way to prove ownership (anything signed by validator key is sus); fund dev of tools to prove ownership and maintain secured dot txt (dot json more likely :)); fund audit of those tools; fund consensus client integrations. And then do an outreach push to convince node runners to deploy this, including big outfits like coinbase, kraken, lido, rocketpool, Blox, allnodes, etc etc If it’s two doods with two validators each the required funds may be out of reach; if the impacted group is larger and/or has more funds staked, they may well jump at the chance to secure those funds > The work for people who are worried would be to propose a mechanism that allows them to verify they are legit, maybe by showing control of the deposit wallet. And then the dot txt could be restricting the 00->01 change to just the eoa of the deposit wallet. Hmm, this is sort of the opposite direction of my original thinking. You're saying to set up a website where people can submit "I own pubkey X, deposit address Y, and this is the tx hash of my deposit" messages? I'd like to avoid a central website if at all possible, but it's going to be hard to make a single txt/json out of these messages otherwise. And also everyone that runs the file should still check with their EL client that the tx is correct. I am not in private contact with any no, but you can see from the links I posted they exist. Many I assume are just not sure if they lost sole-ownership, not necessarily that they _know_ they did. So I'm mostly just trying to work out what a possible solution would look like that they could center around. My thinking was a little different to yours though: 1a) There is a period of time where 0x00 -> 0x01 messages are being accepted by CL clients, but before they can be included on-chain and/or 1b) There is a (low) limit to the number of 0x00 -> 0x01 credential switches in a block. 2) CL client have to rebroadcast **and store/cache** (important assumption!) these messages for later inclusion. 3) CL clients have to do _something_ locally when multiple competing message arrive (even it is just "pick the last one" or "ignore all but the first") 4) Have a json map/dict of _all_ pubkey -> deposit addresses, and then the CL client can have an eviction strategy like "overwrite unless existing messages matches json file" The latter can be generated by a script that everyone can run against their own EL client. Well the challenge I see is that 1) this needs to be seamless for node operators and 2) it needs to function in such a way that an attacker is at a distinct disadvantage. What that looks like exactly is the work that hypothetical group of impacted people would work on / fund. The biggest challenges I see is that this all has to work _before_ credential changes are accepted on the beacon chain, and that node operators have to be convinced to use the option (because it's opt-in). Especially the latter might deter those affected from trying to tackle the first challenge. Yep
